hello iris i'm sending the venue notes before i forget the details the hall is available on february twenty second no february twenty third and the quoted hire period is from ten am until four pm the caretaker said we could arrive earlier to unload but didn't give an exact time so please don't tell the team that access starts at nine new paragraph points to confirm the location of the accessible entrance the number of chairs included and whether we can use the kitchen end of list the kitchen was described as in double quotes available by arrangement close quotes and i don't know whether that means a separate charge the hire fee is two hundred and eighty dollars and the deposit is fifty dollars we need to keep those figures separate because the deposit might be included in the final payment rather than charged on top on another topic the organiser asked whether we could provide microphones i haven't agreed to that yet because our own equipment hasn't been tested since last summer please leave it as a question rather than turning it into a promise i'll speak to the caretaker again once we have the revised booking form thanks harriet

Hello Iris,

I'm sending the venue notes before I forget the details. The hall is available on February 23, and the quoted hire period is from 10 am until 4 pm. The caretaker said we could arrive earlier to unload but didn't give an exact time, so please don't tell the team that access starts at 9.

Points to confirm:

- The location of the accessible entrance
- The number of chairs included
- Whether we can use the kitchen

The kitchen was described as "available by arrangement," and I don't know whether that means a separate charge. The hire fee is $280, and the deposit is $50. We need to keep those figures separate because the deposit might be included in the final payment rather than charged on top.

On another topic, the organiser asked whether we could provide microphones. I haven't agreed to that yet because our own equipment hasn't been tested since last summer. Please leave it as a question rather than turning it into a promise. I'll speak to the caretaker again once we have the revised booking form.

Thanks,
Harriet

the export failed on the large file but succeeded on the smaller sample i don't want the issue title to say that export is completely broken because that would hide the difference between the two cases the error message is in double quotes response exceeded limit close quotes and the field named maxOutputBytes was set to one thousand twenty four i haven't checked whether that limit is applied before or after compression new paragraph the reproduction steps are one load the full archive two choose the json export option three keep the default settings four save the response headers with the error log end of list please don't change the limit during this run because i want to preserve the original conditions we can try a higher limit in a separate comparison afterward on another topic the sample file contains the identifier BatchID with that exact casing and the value zero zero zero seven don't convert the identifier to snake case or drop the leading zeros when writing the note those details may matter to the importer i don't know whether they caused this failure but removing them would make it harder to reproduce what happened

The export failed on the large file but succeeded on the smaller sample. I don't want the issue title to say that export is completely broken because that would hide the difference between the two cases. The error message is "response exceeded limit," and the field named maxOutputBytes was set to 1,024. I haven't checked whether that limit is applied before or after compression.

The reproduction steps are:

1. Load the full archive.
2. Choose the JSON export option.
3. Keep the default settings.
4. Save the response headers with the error log.

Please don't change the limit during this run because I want to preserve the original conditions. We can try a higher limit in a separate comparison afterward.

On another topic, the sample file contains the identifier BatchID with that exact casing and the value 0007. Don't convert the identifier to snake case or drop the leading zeros when writing the note. Those details may matter to the importer. I don't know whether they caused this failure, but removing them would make it harder to reproduce what happened.
